title: Two-way lookup with VLOOKUP and MATCH

screens.prompt: In C6, return the units for the product in A6 and the quarter in B6, using VLOOKUP and letting MATCH find the column.

hints.func-vlookup: VLOOKUP does the fetching. It needs the product, the table, and the number MATCH hands it.
hints.func-match: MATCH takes three arguments: the quarter, the header A1:C1, and 0 for exact. Two arguments is a missing-argument error.
hints.require-ref: Point MATCH at B6. A typed "Q2" answers this one question only.
hints.match-exact: MATCH's third argument must be 0 or FALSE; anything else approximates, which assumes the header is sorted.
hints.value: Both positions count from the Product column. MATCH returns 3 for Q2, and VLOOKUP counts 3 columns into A1:C5.
hints.error: #N/A means a key missed, #REF! means the column number overshot the table, #VALUE! means text reached a numeric slot.
hints.match-type: FALSE as VLOOKUP's fourth argument, or approximate match settles on a row of its own choosing.

accept: =VLOOKUP( A6 , A1:C5 , MATCH( B6 , A1:C1 , 0 ) , FALSE )

reject.why: the right answer with the wrong function
the column number typed in, which breaks when a quarter is inserted
MATCH without the 0, so it is a two-argument call
the quarter typed into the formula instead of read from B6
approximate MATCH on an unsorted header, which can land on any column
MATCH counted from B, so its 2 came out as Q1
approximate VLOOKUP, which stops on the last row it saw
#VALUE!: the column number became the text 3x
the word no where TRUE or FALSE belongs, so the match mode is unreadable

docs.explain:
MATCH finds Q2 in the header A1:C1 and returns 3, the third cell of that range. VLOOKUP takes that 3 as its column number, finds Widget on row 3 of A1:C5, and returns the third value there, 110.

No digit in the formula describes the table. Change B6 to Q1 and the answer becomes 90 with no edit; insert a quarter in the middle and the formula follows it. Type the 3 yourself and neither holds.

The two ranges have to start on the same column. MATCH counts from the first cell it is given, while VLOOKUP counts from its table's left edge. Point MATCH at B1:C1 and its 2 lands on Q1.

errors.text: The quarter is not in the header, or the product is not in the first column.
The MATCH position was joined to text, so VLOOKUP was handed a column number it cannot count with.
MATCH's column number is wider than A1:C5, which happens when its header starts before the table does.

docs.atWork: Units by product and quarter, headcount by team and month: the column you need is itself a lookup.
docs.outcome: Return one cell of a grid from a row key and a column key.

seo.title: Two-way lookup with VLOOKUP and MATCH
seo.description: MATCH turns the quarter into a column number, so no digit in the formula describes the table. Move B6 from Q2 to Q1 and the answer moves from 110 to 90.
